title: Proofing Table
prompt: Create a high-fidelity 1440x900 desktop web application UI composition for Curbcut, a browser-native accessibility repair workbench. This must look like a real professional developer tool screenshot, not a poster or marketing page. Precision-light visual world: cool white drafting-table ground, white working fields, charcoal ink, cobalt blue selection, amber proposal proof marks, emerald verification, restrained red severity; no gradients, no neon, no glass, no excessive rounded cards. Composition option C, Proofing Table: a compact command strip across the top. The three-pane workspace fills the screen like a digital proofing table: left source editor with numbered HTML and exact selection, center live checkout rendering framed by a narrow revision ruler with Working/Proposed tabs, and right remediation evidence organized as a proof sheet with a selected issue, factual axe evidence, mapped source range, and a surgical redline diff. Use understated crop/registration-mark-inspired locator ticks only as functional synchronization markers, not decoration. A bottom action timeline reads as a concise proof log with agent and human entries. Show real Curbcut content including missing label, positive tabindex, image alternative, accessible button name, document language, Not applied, Approve exact change, Reject, and Rescan verified. Professional, dense, accessible, flat, crisp 1px lines and small-radius controls. No chatbot, no marketing page, no ornamental imagery.
